title: Magnet: We Never Know How Text-to-Image Diffusion Models Work, Until We Learn How Vision-Language Models Function
role: Text-embedding-only fix that locates leakage in CLIP's end-of-text and padding tokens; cheap and box-free, but built around adjective-noun pairs, so it has nothing to act on for two bare animal names
enters: text encoder: the end-of-text and padding embeddings blend all concepts, and through cross-attention their maps cover both objects
enters_evidence: one embedding measurement (60 objects x 7 colours, word vs end-of-text cosine) plus image demonstrations: embedding swaps, end-of-text-to-padding cosine falling from 1.0 to about 0.7, padding attention covering both objects; the link to leakage is argued from single examples
changes: each object's word embedding before sampling: c_hat = c + alpha * v_pos - beta * v_neg, vectors averaged over the 5 nearest neighbour nouns, strengths from the end-of-text vs last-padding cosine; used at every step
training: nothing trained; needs the Stanza dependency parser for adjective-noun pairs and a 614-noun candidate list made with ChatGPT and checked by hand; no boxes, masks or reference image
model: SD1.4 (CLIP ViT-L/14), 50 steps, guidance 7.5; FID on SD2.1; one qualitative image each on SD2.1, SDXL, PixArt
similar_subjects: no per-type result: CC-500 subset built as 80 prompts each of two living, one living one non-living, two non-living objects (240 prompts), but tables pool them; two-animal prompts shown only as single images
which_pairs: noun-noun CLIP word-embedding cosine is computed only to pick 5 neighbour nouns and is never related to binding failure; the paper ties failure to attribute bias and to drift between the end-of-text and last padding embedding (omega peaks at 0.66 and 0.71 over 19,648 prompts), without counting failures against either
when: not measured; the limitations guess that the colour layout is determined in the early stage
cost: no extra UNet passes; 6.81 s per image against 6.62 s for SD1.4 (+2.9%); neighbour step adds 0.25 s per image at K = 5
headline: CC-500 human attribute alignment on SD1.4: 74.0% for Magnet against 66.2% for Attend-and-Excite and 59.1% for plain SD, at 6.81 s against 6.62 s per image
suggests: (inferred) swap a name-cosine predictor for padding-token attention overlap or end-of-text drift; as a fix it changes nothing on two bare animal names, but its padding claim suggests swapping the joint prompt's padding embeddings for single-subject ones inside CO3
